title: Cantilever with axial and lateral end load: compression and tension

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.location: Example 8.4, Equations e and g (the member of Example 9.4)
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Plane (x-y) problem of the source modelled in 3D with the global Y axis vertical, so that the source's x, y and theta_z are the model's X, Y and rz. In-plane bending is about local z for every member (default orientation), hence the source's I is the section's Iz. The source gives in closed form the tip deflection of a cantilever under a vertical load P and a horizontal load alpha P at the tip: Delta = alpha L [tan(kL)/(kL) - 1] for P downward (Eq. e) and Delta = alpha L [1 - tanh(kL)/(kL)] for P upward (Eq. g), k = sqrt(P/EI). Numeric instance: the member of Example 9.4 (L = 4 m, A = 1.27e4 mm^2, I = 3.66e7 mm^4, E = 200,000 MPa, alpha = 0.005) with P = 600 kN (combination C, compression) and P = 5000 kN (combination T, tension) chosen here; the source shows these responses only as curves. Second-order analysis, one member, no shear deformation. Plane stability problem: the source's model has no out-of-plane degrees of freedom. Here the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held and Iy = 1000 Iz, so that no out-of-plane buckling mode precedes the in-plane modes compared; J is a placeholder.
